partners.diseaseBName: neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, short stature, and speech delay
partners.mechanism_chain: COL7A1 (HGNC:2207) —DISRUPTS→ Protein folding and trafficking (GO:0006457); Protein folding and trafficking (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (MONDO:0009179); TRAPPC10 (HGNC:20030) —DISRUPTS→ Protein folding and trafficking (GO:0006457); Protein folding and trafficking (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Collagen fibril organization (GO:0030199); Collagen fibril organization (GO:0030199) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, short stature, and speech delay (MONDO:0859285). Loss-of-function mutations in COL7A1 disrupt collagen VII production, essential for anchoring the epidermis, leading to dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Simultaneously, loss-of-function mutations in TRAPPC10 impair protein trafficking and folding, which can indirectly affect the organization and function of extracellular matrix components, including collagen, and potentially lead to developmental defects characteristic of neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, short stature, and speech delay. Both pathways converge on the integrity of protein folding and extracellular matrix organization.

For instance, enhancing protein trafficking pathways might offer a strategy to improve collagen processing in RDEB, or conversely, supporting extracellular matrix integrity could ameliorate skeletal abnormalities in SED T. Identifying shared downstream pathways could lead to treatments applicable to both conditions.
